know (imperative)

and in your fortunes, know, I share your grief, where 'know' is inserted in the middle of the sentence as 'I know well' in the places indicated above, and likewise 'know well' or 'for know well' in the places to be indicated below.
know this well – lest you speak twice.
for know this well, never in a single day may so great a number of men die.
know this well now, the evil is not yet at its height.
know well that for the sake of the multitude the barbarians prevailed with their ships.
know, hearing the truth.
know that I will not corrupt my judgment.
but know that you are wretched from a bold spirit.
cast out by the people, know well, curses that will be stoned.
know that you will pay me recompense.
he will lift, know well, and cast upon your eyes.
know that you are the orphaned foal of a dear man yoked.
for know, whichever of these you establish for your children and house, it remains.
from these then, know, there is a fine device.
let him know, whoever has not learned, winged by anxieties.
for know well, my son – he would be a wondrous man.
